newsitem.title: CANADA: Some NW Prairie crops face spring harvest -Pioneer.
newsitem.headline: Some NW Prairie crops face spring harvest -Pioneer.

text.p: Many fields in the northwest of Canada's Prairies may remain with standing crops until spring because of snow reported across the region, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in a crop report for the week ended Oct 23.
Harvest was at a virtual standstill because of wet weather in British Columbia's Dawson Creek region with 15 percent of crops. More snow and rain were forecast for the region.
Weather interrupted harvest in Alberta's Peace River Valley with 20 to 25 percent of crops combined to date.
Harvest in both regions should end next week with standing crops remaining until spring before they can be combined.
Alberta's harvest was complete in the south and 60 percent done in the north.
Nothern Saskatchewan had harvested 90 percent of crops in the west and central parts of the region and 70 percent in the east. Flax, however, was only 35 percent harvested north of Saskatoon.
Southwest Saskatchewan had five percent of the crop left to harvest.
Southeast Saskatchewan had harvested 90 percent of its crops. Snow was reported in many parts of the region.
Eastern Saskatchewan harvested 85 percent of its crops while Manitoba was 95 percent done. Some areas reported up to 10 inches of snow in the past week, some of which accumulated on the ground.
